news.headline: uniQure stock holds recent gains as Huntington's gene therapy filing reshapes outlook
news.summary: uniQure shares were holding near $44, roughly 84% above where they started 2026, as the recent BLA and UK MHRA filings for AMT-130 continued to support investor sentiment. Coverage framed the filings as having reshaped the near-term outlook for the stock ahead of the pending four-year data readout.

news.headline: uniQure stock eyes key AMT-130 update as Huntington's gene therapy advances
news.summary: The article highlighted that investors were positioning ahead of uniQure's guided four-year AMT-130 topline data update, expected before the end of September 2026, following the company's BLA submission to the FDA and MAA filing with the UK MHRA. It noted the stock's strong multi-month run as anticipation built for the readout.

news.headline: What to expect from UniQure's upcoming Huntington's gene therapy readout
news.summary: STAT previewed uniQure's closely watched four-year AMT-130 data update, which will cover 12 high-dose and 12 low-dose patients (plus three additional high-dose patients at three years), benchmarked against an expanded ~26,000-patient Enroll-HD natural-history comparator. The piece noted the prior three-year analysis showed roughly 75% slower disease progression in the high-dose group, while flagging a disappointing readout, an FDA advisory committee, or confirmatory-trial requirements as the key risks that could still delay or derail approval.

news.headline: Analysts Set uniQure N.V. (NASDAQ:QURE) Price Target at $65.00
news.summary: The average 12-month price target among the 17 brokerages covering uniQure rose to about $65, with a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating (14 buy, 2 hold, 1 sell). The upgrade wave reflected growing Wall Street optimism following the AMT-130 BLA and MAA filings and ahead of the pending four-year data readout.

news.headline: uniQure (NASDAQ:QURE) Downgraded by Wall Street Zen to Sell
news.summary: Wall Street Zen cut its rating on uniQure from Hold to Sell, citing the stock's steep run-up into the pending four-year AMT-130 data and a valuation that had become disconnected from near-term fundamentals. The downgrade stood out against a broader wave of sell-side price-target increases from other brokerages around the same time.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Submission of Biologics License Application for Ifezuntirgene Inilparvovec (AMT-130) in Huntington's Disease
news.summary: uniQure submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA seeking accelerated approval of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) for Huntington's disease and requested priority review, while also filing a Marketing Authorisation Application with the UK's MHRA. The submissions are supported by three-year Phase I/II data benchmarked against a propensity-matched Enroll-HD external control, and AMT-130 already holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy and RMAT designations. Separately, William Blair initiated coverage of uniQure the same day with an Outperform rating.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 topline data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure has guided that four-year (48-month) follow-up data on the Phase I/II Huntington's disease study (12 high-dose and 12 low-dose patients, plus 3 additional high-dose patients at three years), benchmarked against an expanded ~26,000-patient Enroll-HD comparator, will be released before the end of Q3 2026. As of September 24, 2026 this data has still not been announced, with only days remaining before the guided deadline, making it the single biggest near-term binary catalyst for the stock.

catalysts.label: FDA BLA filing acceptance decision
catalysts.detail: Following the September 2, 2026 BLA submission, the FDA is expected to complete its standard 60-day filing review to decide whether to formally accept the application and grant the requested priority review; no acceptance decision or PDUFA date had been announced as of September 24, 2026.

catalysts.when: Likely H1 2027 (if BLA accepted for priority review)
catalysts.label: Potential FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: uniQure's leadership has said an AdCom is likely given AMT-130 would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease, and the company says it is preparing for one, but no meeting has been scheduled or dated.

catalysts.label: FDA target action date for accelerated approval
catalysts.detail: If the FDA accepts the BLA under priority review, uniQure has indicated an action date could fall in late April or early May 2027, which would make AMT-130 potentially the first approved disease-modifying Huntington's therapy.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA MAA decision on AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure filed a Marketing Authorisation Application with the UK MHRA in parallel with the FDA BLA (submitted around September 2, 2026); a specific MHRA review completion or decision date has not been disclosed.

catalysts.label: Third-quarter 2026 financial results
catalysts.detail: uniQure's next scheduled quarterly earnings report, which should provide updated commentary on regulatory timelines, cash runway, and reaction to the four-year data readout.

pulse: uniQure remains suspended ahead of biotech's biggest pending binary event: four-year AMT-130 Huntington's disease data guided for release before September 30, 2026, which as of today (September 24) still has not been reported, with only days left on that guidance. This follows a September 2 BLA filing (with priority review requested) to the FDA and a parallel MAA filing with the UK MHRA, both built on three-year data showing roughly 75% slower disease progression at the high dose; the stock has pulled back into the low-to-mid $40s from its recent highs as the wait drags on. Sentiment remains split into the readout, with a wave of sell-side price-target hikes and a William Blair Outperform initiation offset by a Wall Street Zen downgrade to Sell on valuation grounds, while an FDA advisory committee and an unresolved confirmatory post-marketing trial design remain overhangs even if the BLA is ultimately accepted.
